Torty Text for Mac · by Marc Hedlund

Type a few letters. Torty types the rest.

A small, friendly snippet expander that lives in your menu bar. Type a short abbreviation in any app and it becomes your full signature, reply, link or block of code. Slow and steady, but your typing won't be.

A closer look

These are screenshots of the real app in light mode, with sample snippets.

Abbreviations that expand anywhere

Give a snippet a short abbreviation like zsig or ;date. Type it in Mail, Slack, a browser or your code editor and it's replaced on the spot, with a soft pop so you know it worked.

  • Plain text and rich text with bold, links and images
  • A toolbar that inserts every snippet code for you
  • A warning when two abbreviations would clash

Search from anywhere

Press Control Option Space in any app to find a snippet by name or content. It goes right back where your cursor was, even a browser's address bar.

  • Recent snippets first, ⌘1 to ⌘9 to insert
  • Make a snippet from what you just copied
  • Jump to the last snippet you used

Reports and time saved

Torty's home screen shows how much typing you've skipped, as Daily, Weekly or Monthly reports, plus your most used snippets. Click Torty for a joke, a word of the day or a turtle fact.

Groups with their own rules

Keep snippets in groups, and decide where each group works: only at the start of a word, only in certain apps or websites, or everywhere except some.

Fill-ins and optional sections

A snippet can ask for a name first, offer a list of choices, or include a section only if you tick it, like a PS or a disclaimer.

Settings, profile and help

Your name and email live in My Profile and drop into any snippet. Help, Submit an Idea and Check for Updates are one click away.

Snippet codes

Put these inside any snippet. A plain % always stays a %, so AMPscript, Liquid and CSS come through exactly as written.

[[cursor]]Leave the cursor here
[[clipboard]]Whatever text is on your clipboard
[[date]]Today's date, like 2026-11-01
[[date:%B %e, %Y]]Any format, like November 1, 2026
[[date:+3d:%A]]Date math: d, w, m, y, or H, M, S
[[time]]The current time
[[name]] [[email]]From My Profile
[[key:tab]]Press a key: tab, return, esc, arrows
[[snippet:zsig]]Include another snippet
[[filltext:name=First name]]Ask for a value before expanding
[[fillarea:name=Notes]]Ask for a longer value
[[fillpopup:name=Tone:default=Friendly:Formal]]Pick from a list
[[fillpart:name=PS]]…[[/fillpart]]Optional section with a checkbox

Getting set up

For Macs with Apple silicon (M1 or newer) on macOS 11 or later. The full steps are in the README that comes with the app.

  1. Install

    Unzip the file and drag Torty Text into your Applications folder.

  2. Open it once

    macOS blocks it the first time. Go to System Settings, then Privacy & Security, and click Open Anyway.

  3. Allow keyboard access

    In Privacy & Security, then Accessibility, turn on Torty Text. Quit and reopen it, and you're ready to type.

If macOS says the app "is damaged", open Terminal, run this line, then open the app again: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Torty Text.app"
